declared_purpose: Manage TickTick tasks and projects through a CLI with OAuth2 authentication, batch operations and rate-limit handling (SKILL.md:2–8). Agent instructions require JSON output, listing projects first and checking status before completion, and recommend project IDs (SKILL.md:172–179).

data_operations.operation: Read command-line inputs and dispatch commands
data_operations.data_scope: OAuth client credentials, task/project identifiers, task text, tags, priorities, dates and project properties
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI process; the shell wrapper forwards arguments to Bun
data_operations.condition: When the corresponding command is invoked

data_operations.data_scope: clientId, clientSecret, accessToken, refreshToken, tokenExpiry and redirectUri
data_operations.condition: Authentication setup, authentication flows, token acquisition, status checks and logout. Every API request obtains a token through getValidToken. Status checks may refresh an expiring token.

data_operations.operation: Persist credentials and tokens in plaintext JSON
data_operations.source: Supplied OAuth credentials and TickTick token responses
data_operations.data_scope: Client credentials, access/refresh tokens, calculated expiry and redirect URI; credential setup preserves existing configuration fields
data_operations.condition: Credential setup, successful authentication or refresh. Directory/file modes are requested as 700/600; chmod failures are suppressed. Persistence is documented; this file-based implementation is a design choice.

data_operations.operation: Construct and print an OAuth authorization URL; attempt browser opening
data_operations.source: Saved clientId and redirectUri, plus newly generated random state
data_operations.data_scope: Client ID, state, redirect URI, response type and tasks:read/tasks:write scopes
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout; automatic flow passes the URL to the open dependency. TickTick's https://ticktick.com/oauth/authorize receives it if visited.
data_operations.condition: Both authentication modes print the URL; only automatic mode attempts to open it

data_operations.operation: Receive and validate an OAuth redirect
data_operations.source: Browser callback or pasted redirect URL
data_operations.data_scope: Authorization code, state and OAuth error; manual mode initially reads the full supplied URL
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory. Automatic callback listens on 127.0.0.1 and returns success/failure HTML to the requesting browser; OAuth error text is reflected in failure HTML and an exception.
data_operations.condition: Automatic mode accepts the root callback and validates state; manual mode reads stdin and validates state/code. The automatic listener closes on handled success/failure or timeout.

data_operations.operation: Exchange authorization codes or refresh tokens
data_operations.source: Saved client credentials and received code or refreshToken
data_operations.data_scope: Basic-auth client credentials; authorization code and redirect URI, or refresh token. Responses supply accessToken, refreshToken and expiry.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: HTTPS POST to https://ticktick.com/oauth/token; response returns to the authentication component and is saved locally
data_operations.condition: Code exchange follows either authentication mode. Refresh occurs within five minutes of expiry when a refreshToken exists, including through auth --status.

data_operations.data_scope: accessToken, refreshToken and tokenExpiry are removed; client credentials and other configuration remain
data_operations.condition: auth --logout. Keeping credentials is explicitly documented. The function does not request remote token revocation or unlink the configuration file.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate API requests, parse responses and retry rate-limited requests
data_operations.source: getValidToken, API method arguments and TickTick responses
data_operations.data_scope: Bearer access token, endpoint identifiers, applicable JSON payloads and response bodies
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.ticktick.com/open/v1; parsed responses return to the calling component
data_operations.condition: Every API method. Recognized rate-limit failures cause up to four retries with the same endpoint/options, including mutation requests.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve the project catalog and resolve projects locally
data_operations.data_scope: Unprojected project response objects, typed to include IDs, names, color, ordering, closed state, grouping, view, permission and kind
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local API/command process; names and IDs are compared locally
data_operations.condition: Project listing, project resolution and task searches/listing. Exported getInboxData and getAllTasks also enumerate projects. Listing projects first is an explicit agent instruction; repeated internal enumeration is an implementation choice.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve project task datasets and search/filter locally
data_operations.source: TickTick GET /project/{projectId}/data; exported inbox helper can use /project/inbox/data
data_operations.data_scope: Project data and unprojected task records, potentially including text, dates, status, priority, timezone, reminders, tags and checklist items
data_operations.condition: Task listing and target resolution for update/complete/abandon/batch-abandon. ID lookup stops at the first hit; title lookup collects matches across selected projects. Listing status filters run after retrieval. Inaccessible projects are skipped.

data_operations.operation: Derive dates from supplied date expressions
data_operations.source: Caller due-date input and the local clock/calendar
data_operations.data_scope: Computed dueDate; relative dates use local calendar operations and are serialized as UTC timestamps. Display code also derives today/tomorrow labels.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory and caller output; computed dueDate enters the requested TickTick task write
data_operations.condition: --due on task creation/update, or displaying a task with a due date

data_operations.operation: Request task creation, changes, completion or abandonment
data_operations.source: Caller inputs and resolved task/project IDs
data_operations.data_scope: Creation sends title/projectId and supplied content, priority, dueDate and tags. CLI updates send IDs and explicitly set fields. Completion sends IDs in the URL. Abandonment sends status -1; batch abandonment sends ID/projectId/status tuples.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: TickTick /task, /task/{id}, /project/{projectId}/task/{taskId}/complete or /batch/task; requested changes concern remote task records
data_operations.condition: Corresponding CLI command after target resolution. Abandonment is a status update, not a deletion request.

data_operations.source: Caller project name/color and resolved project ID
data_operations.data_scope: Creation sends name and optional normalized color; update sends ID and supplied name/color
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: TickTick POST /project or /project/{id}; requested changes concern remote project records
data_operations.condition: list command in create or update mode

data_operations.source: Arguments supplied to the exported API object
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: TickTick DELETE /project/{projectId}/task/{taskId}, or a delete array in POST /batch/task
data_operations.condition: A programmatic caller invokes deleteTask or supplies batch deletion entries. Actual server deletion and retention are undocumented.

data_operations.operation: Return task/project results to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: JSON mode returns project/task response objects; task listings add projectName. Completion returns a selected success/task object. Batch abandonment returns IDs, notFound and the batch response. Text mode emits summaries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout; no additional recipient or durable output storage is specified
data_operations.condition: Successful commands; JSON output is explicitly required for agent use

data_operations.source: Remote error bodies, local search results and invalid manual-auth input
data_operations.data_scope: Generic API errors include raw response text; token-exchange exceptions include raw error bodies; ambiguous-title errors include task titles, shortened IDs and project names; invalid manual redirects are included in exceptions
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Exceptions returned to callers; command catch handlers print error messages to stderr. Authentication exception handling beyond the supplied action remains unspecified.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second retrieval of the complete project catalog
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: TickTick receives another authenticated GET /project; its response enters local CLI memory
potential_excess.condition: tasks --list first calls listProjects, then findProjectByName calls listProjects again
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Resolve the selected project and list its tasks. The initial project listing satisfies the explicit agent instruction.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the matching project and preserve project-name mapping
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the redundant catalog request by resolving against the already fetched projects
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the existing case-insensitive name and exact-ID matching behavior and project-not-found handling

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated project catalogs and overlapping full project task datasets
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Repeated authenticated requests to TickTick; repeated responses enter local CLI memory
potential_excess.condition: batch-abandon calls findTaskById separately for every supplied task ID
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Resolve project IDs and submit one batch status update
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve each target ID and report unresolved IDs before submitting the batch
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve all target IDs in one invocation-scoped traversal, fetching each needed project once and stopping when all targets are found
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve target/project mappings, notFound reporting and handling of inaccessible projects; keep any necessary retry behavior

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated task records and fields such as content, descriptions, reminders, tags and checklist items during single-task resolution
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: TickTick project-data responses enter the local API/CLI process
potential_excess.condition: Lookup preceding task update, completion, abandonment or batch abandonment
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Identify the target and project, detect title ambiguity and make status available for the required completion check
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain identifying fields, relevant status and enough matching information to select the correct task
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse validated project information and limit searches to a supplied project. If supported by TickTick, use direct task retrieval or field projection to reduce extra records/fields in the required read.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve unscoped title ambiguity detection and status availability. The supplied source establishes only bulk project-data retrieval, so remote payload reduction remains conditional on undocumented API capabilities.

potential_excess.data_scope: The complete pasted redirect URL, potentially containing an authorization code, state and additional query data
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Thrown manual-auth exception available to the caller/runtime
potential_excess.condition: URL parsing, state validation or code validation fails
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Validate the OAuth response and explain authentication failure
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reject invalid input and report a useful reason
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the redirect URL from the exception; report a sanitized parsing/state/code error
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep mandatory state equality and authorization-code checks

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrestricted remote error-body text; any sensitive content depends on the undocumented response
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: API/auth exceptions; API command handlers can copy the message to caller stderr
potential_excess.condition: A generic API failure or token-exchange failure returns details beyond those needed to report failure
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Explain unsuccessful task operations or authentication
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Report failure, HTTP status and a useful sanitized explanation
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Limit default error output to status and sanitized diagnostics; make additional redacted detail optional
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve rate-limit/authentication handling and actionable errors. Actual sensitive error-body contents are unresolved.

unknowns: Blocking remote-read minimization assessment: the supplied source does not establish direct-task endpoints, field projection or server-side status filtering. Whether complete project datasets are unavoidable remains unresolved.

TickTick's actual response/error fields, effective authorization scope, retention, logging, token invalidation and deletion semantics are undocumented here; requested remote changes do not establish permanent deletion.

Dependency implementations and browser, shell, runtime or caller capture/persistence behavior are outside the supplied source. Passing URLs, arguments or normal results to these components does not establish further disclosure or retention.

Actual filesystem permission enforcement, residual recoverability after configuration rewrites and runtime behavior were not verified. All supplied package files were reviewed; these external behaviors remain unresolved.
